<h2>Inupiaq</h2>

```{=html}
<div class="main-content">

<!--- PARAGRAPH 1 --->
<div class="text-image-row">
  
  <div class="text-lines">
    
    <div class="my-hover">
      IỊaatnigguuq Aviññaq puuvruuraqtuq.
      
      <div class="my-hover-text">
        <p><strong> IỊaatnigguuq Aviññaq puuvruu-raq-tuq. </strong></p>
        
        <p> Stem "puuvruu" means "to swim". </p>
        
        <p> Ending "raq" is a past tense marker. </p>
        
        <p> Ending "tuq" is for intransitive, indicative, third-person singular. Notice that "tuq" is used when following a consonant, and "ruq" is used when following a vowel. </p> 
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<!--- PARAGRAPH 2 --->
<div class="text-image-row">

  <div class="text-lines">
  
    <div class="my-hover">
      lkaaġaa kuuk.
      
      <div class="my-hover-text">
        <p><strong> lkaaq-ġaa kuuk. </strong></p>
        
        <p> Stem "ikaaq" means to cross. </p>
        
        <p> Ending "ġaa" is for transitive, indicative verbs. Since both arguments (the subject and the object) are third-person, -a is added to +k/ga. </p>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<!--- PARAGRAPH 3 --->

  <div class="text-lines">

      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

::: {#side-panel .side-panel}
<h2>English</h2>

<p><strong> The Mouse Story by Arthur Douglas Sr. </strong></p>

<p> It is said that once upon a time, Mouse was swimming. </p>

<p> He crossed a river. </p>

<p> After he had crossed it, he looked back and proudly remarked, </p>

<p> "I have crossed the great big river all by myself." </p> 

<p> Actually, what had happened was that he had crossed a person's footprint in soft mud which was filled with water. </p>
:::

```{=html}
<button class="toggle-button" id="toggle-button" onclick="togglePanel()">

›

</button>
```

:::::

```{=html}
<!-- This is javascript -->
<script>

function togglePanel() {

<!-- find the two panel container and... -->
const container = document.getElementById("two-panel");

<!-- allow for the container to be open or collapsed --> 
container.classList.toggle("collapsed");

<!-- find the button and... -->
const button = document.getElementById("toggle-button");

<!-- change the direction of the arrow if open or collapsed -->
if (container.classList.contains("collapsed")) {
button.textContent = "‹";
} else {
button.textContent = "›";
}
}

</script>
```
